narrative.overview: A dark, materially rich engineering portfolio staged the way Apple stages a product: one confident chrome language, a single glowing accent per act, everything else standing back. A twisted glossy 3D ring anchors the scroll — it is not decoration, it is the exhibit, changing color as the visitor moves through six acts. The interface behaves like glass and metal on a stage, not like a document.
keyCharacteristics: True-black stage with cool space-gray hardware and a rotating single-hue glow per section
Translucent frosted glass on every floating surface (nav, cards, lightbox) — never two stacked
Bold, tightly-tracked sans display type; no serif anywhere
Instant, physical press feedback on every interactive element

rules.name: The One Glow Rule
rules.body: Exactly one accent hue is active per section, carried by the ring and mirrored in that section's labels. Two accent hues never appear as equals in the same viewport.

rules.name: The Negative Tracking Rule
rules.body: Tracking tightens as size grows (-0.03em at display scale) and loosens toward neutral at body scale; caps labels get positive tracking (0.14em), not the old 0.42em maximalist spacing.

rules.name: The Glass-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Nav, cards, and the lightbox get their depth from blur + translucency, not shadows. Shadows are reserved for the few elements meant to feel physically lifted off the glass.

dos: Do keep exactly one accent hue live per section, mirrored between the ring glow and that section's labels.
Do build every floating surface as translucent glass — backdrop-filter + hairline border, never flat opaque fill.
Do give every clickable element instant :active press feedback (scale 0.975).
Do tighten letter-spacing as type size grows; loosen only on caps labels.
donts: Don't introduce a second display typeface or bring back a serif.
Don't stack two translucent surfaces on top of each other.
Don't let more than one accent color read as dominant in the same viewport.
Don't add drop shadows to glass surfaces as a substitute for blur.
